 FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE October 26, 2026
 Charlottesville Sheriff James Brown Reappointed as National Sheriffs’ Association Committee Chair
 CHARLOTTESVILLE, VA — Charlottesville Sheriff James Brown has been reappointed as Chair of the National Sheriffs’ Association’s (NSA) Court Security, Transportation of Prisoners, and Civil Process Committee, continuing his leadership and contributions to national discussions on law enforcement and public safety.
 Following his reappointment, Sheriff Brown has participated in interviews with Bloomberg and Dateline , discussing the significance of his leadership role and its broader impact. He has also met with representatives from the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) and the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to address national issues surrounding REAL ID.
 In this role, Sheriff Brown serves as a resource and networking connection for sheriff’s offices across the country, facilitating collaboration and the exchange of ideas among agencies. The committee’s work supports the development of consistent practices while allowing individual sheriff’s offices the flexibility to adapt those practices to their jurisdictions’ unique needs and circumstances.
 Sheriff Brown’s reappointment highlights the importance of collaboration among public safety leaders and provides an opportunity to contribute to discussions and solutions addressing challenges that affect sheriff’s offices nationwide.
 Through his continued involvement with the National Sheriffs’ Association, Sheriff Brown will help strengthen professional partnerships, share knowledge, and support efforts to advance effective practices in court security, prisoner transportation, and civil process.
 Media Contact Kyle Ervin Public Safety Information Office City of Charlottesville (434) 326-3043 ervinkl@charlottesville.gov
